title: Truncating a name to a fixed length can cut a letter in half, dropping its accent silently
assumption: Truncating a string to N characters always leaves N valid, complete characters.

input.display: "Nguy\u1ec5n V\u0103n H\u01b0ng" (an invented, common-pattern Vietnamese name) normalized to NFD, truncated to 11 code points
input.description: A name stored in decomposed Unicode form (common after certain input methods or normalization steps) being cut down to fit a fixed-width column or display field.

what_goes_wrong: The cut lands between a base letter and its combining accent mark, silently dropping the accent and turning "Văn" into "Va", with no error, warning, or visible corruption in the truncation step itself.
why: In NFD (decomposed) form, an accented letter like ă is represented as TWO code points: the base letter 'a' followed by a separate combining breve mark. A length-based slice has no concept of 'this code point belongs with the previous one'; it just counts positions, so a cut that lands exactly between the base letter and its combining mark keeps the bare base letter and discards the accent, producing a different, valid-looking string that is quietly wrong rather than visibly broken.
affects: any code-point-count truncation (string slicing, SQL LEFT()/SUBSTRING(), an explicit cast to varchar(n)) applied to NFD text

repros.code:
import unicodedata
name = unicodedata.normalize("NFD", "Nguy\u1ec5n V\u0103n H\u01b0ng")
print("full (NFC):", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", name))
truncated = name[:11]
print("truncated (NFC):", unicodedata.normalize("NFC", truncated))
repros.expected_output:
full (NFC): Nguyễn Văn Hưng
truncated (NFC): Nguyễn Va

full (NFC): Nguyễn Văn Hưng
truncated (NFC): Nguyễn Va

fix: Normalize to NFC before storing or measuring length (precomposed accented letters are single code points, far less likely to be split), and when you must truncate, cut at a grapheme-cluster boundary, not a raw code-point or UTF-16-unit count.

sources.title: Unicode Standard Annex #29: Unicode Text Segmentation (grapheme clusters)
Unicode Standard Annex #15: Unicode Normalization Forms

test_cases.note: Feed your truncation helper this name in NFD form with a limit of 11: a grapheme-aware truncation keeps "Nguyễn V" or "Nguyễn Vă", never a bare "a" stripped of its breve.
